Binary and non-normal outcomes or mediators

Source: vignettes/articles/model-glm-families.qmd

The default engine fits each model with glm(), so the outcome and the mediator can each take a family. Part of the Models collection.

Structure X to M to Y, one model per variable
Class returned MediationData
Set with family_y = and family_m = in fit_mediation(), or fit the glm() yourself and extract
Scale b and c' are on the outcome’s link scale; a is on the mediator’s 
library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union
d <- mediation_demo
d$outcome_bin <- as.integer(d$outcome > median(d$outcome))
d$mediator_bin <- as.integer(d$mediator1 > median(d$mediator1))

Read this first

With a non-identity link, b and c' are on the link scale, so the product a * b is not a natural indirect effect on the outcome scale. medfit reports the product; the interpretation is yours to defend. See Methods and Formulas.

Binary outcome 

fit_y <- fit_mediation(
  outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
  mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,
  data = d, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
  family_y = binomial()
)
paths(fit_y)
        a         b   c_prime
0.5826425 0.8632919 0.1271924

Here b and c' are log odds ratios and a is a change in the mediator.

Binary mediator 

fit_m <- fit_mediation(
  outcome ~ treatment + mediator_bin + covariate1 + covariate2,
  mediator_bin ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,
  data = d, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator_bin",
  family_m = binomial()
)
paths(fit_m)
        a         b   c_prime
1.0525050 0.8880579 0.3334008

Now a is a log odds ratio and b is a change in the outcome per unit of the mediator.

Other families

Any glm() family works the same way, for example a count outcome:

set.seed(1)
d$count <- rpois(nrow(d), exp(0.2 + 0.2 * d$mediator1))
fit_c <- fit_mediation(
  count ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1,
  mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1,
  data = d, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
  family_y = poisson()
)
class(fit_c)[1]
[1] "medfit::MediationData"

Joint significance test for the indirect effect

With a binary or count outcome there is no outcome-scale indirect effect here, but you can still test whether the mediated path exists. For a recursive model with no correlated errors the likelihood factors by equation, so the test reduces to the joint significance test: test a = 0 in the mediator model and b = 0 in the outcome model, and take the larger p-value. The null is “a = 0 or b = 0”, so the test is conservative, like mbco_sem() on the native engine.

joint_test <- function(fit_a, term_a, fit_b, term_b) {
  one <- function(fit, term) {
    known <- fit$family$family %in% c("binomial", "poisson")
    col <- if (known) "Pr(>Chi)" else "Pr(>F)"
    drop1(fit, scope = term, test = if (known) "LRT" else "F")[term, col]
  }
  p <- c(a = one(fit_a, term_a), b = one(fit_b, term_b))
  c(p, joint = max(p))
}
fit_a <- glm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d)
fit_b <- glm(outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
             data = d, family = binomial())
joint_test(fit_a, "treatment", fit_b, "mediator1")
           a            b        joint
8.096703e-09 2.024938e-12 8.096703e-09

The test for each path depends on the family:

  • Known dispersion (binomial, Poisson): a likelihood-ratio test, as above for the binary outcome.
  • Estimated dispersion (Gaussian, Gamma, and every quasi* family): an F test. These families have no likelihood with the dispersion known, so a likelihood-ratio chi-square would be too liberal. The helper switches on the family; the mediator above is Gaussian and gets the F test.

The result is on the link scale, like the paths; it says that the mediated path is detectable, not how large the effect is on the outcome scale. A function that also reports outcome-scale effects is planned.

Limits

  • The four-way and joint decompositions need Gaussian identity-link models and stop with an informative error otherwise.
  • Intervals for the product still come from the delta method or a bootstrap; see Bootstrap Inference.
  • Fitted glm() pairs can be extracted instead of fitted here: extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_y, ...).
